page.overview:
What is Jurassic Park (novel)?

Jurassic Park is a novel written by Michael Crichton, the best-selling author of various other books, such as The Andromeda Strain. Jurassic Park was released on November 20, 1990. It is the first book in the Jurassic Park franchise. In the spring of 1990, an earlier draft of the novel was given to Steven Spielberg, who immediately started the production of a movie adaptation. The movie of the same name was released on June 11, 1993. Crichton published a sequel, The Lost World, on September 8, 1995. which also got a movie adaptation with the same name later in time.

The narrative begins by slowly tying together a series of incidents involving strange animal attacks in Costa Rica and on Isla Nublar, the main setting for the story. In one horrific incident, three Procompsognathus kill and eat a baby at a maternity clinic in the village of Bahía Anasco. Paleontologist Alan Grant and his paleobotanist graduate student Ellie Sattler are visited by Bob Morris, an official with the EPA, who queries Grant about his relationship with the "Hammond Foundation". Shortly thereafter, Grant and Sattler receive a fax containing an X-ray that Grant instantly recognizes.

Before they can act on this knowledge, however, they get a phone call from John Hammond (founder and CEO of "International Genetic Technologies" or InGen) who asks them to take part in a weekend excursion to Isla Nublar, where InGen has set up a private "biological preserve". Secretly, the preserve is in fact "Jurassic Park", which Hammond intends to operate as a zoological amusement park showcasing InGen's new advances in genetic engineering.

Recent events have worried Hammond's considerable investors, so, to placate them, he hires Grant and Sattler to inspect the park as InGen consultants. They stand in counterbalance to a well-known mathematician and chaos theorist, Ian Malcolm, and a lawyer representing the investors, Donald Gennaro. Both are pessimistic, but Malcolm, having been consulted before the park's creation, is emphatic in his prediction that the park will collapse, as it is an unsustainable simple structure bluntly forced upon a complex system.

Also known as: Jurassic Park book.
